title: Every clarinetist once had his own sound
summary: Barnes says he wants to sound only like himself, and that today's players sound more alike.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You want to do like other guys do and let the whole lot know. I believe. I'm telling the truth in all my things. I'm joking. I don't care what to do, I don't like a none of man's style. I wouldn't want anybody to say that I sound like him. I sound like myself, do like myself. That's why you see I play clarinet. I play a lot different clarinet from myself. You know the same, you're going to sit good.
Well back in the old days were the clarinet players all sounding different or were they sounding alike?
Well I tell you artists most of them would have their songs.
Every man would have their songs to play. Would you say that there's less of that now, that the musicians sound more alike now?
To me they sound more alike than everything else. Some of them just got a natural tone and some others got a real tone.
